annotation.kind: Audit 1 repair preserving compatible rectangular dimensions and the explicit Frobenius norm in Section 2.1

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P15 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P15 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p15_t1_frobenius_submultiplicative {m n p : Nat} (A : P15RectMatrix m n) (B : P15RectMatrix n p) : p15RectFrobNorm (p15RectMatMul A B) <= p15RectFrobNorm A * p15RectFrobNorm B
formal_statement.plain_language: For every pair of compatible finite rectangular real matrices, the Frobenius norm of their product is at most the product of their Frobenius norms.

informal_proof: Identify the explicit square-root-of-sums definition and finite compatible product with the corresponding rectangular Frobenius objects, then apply constant-one Frobenius submultiplicativity.
informal_statement: The first Frobenius-norm property listed in Section 2.1 for arbitrary multiplication-compatible rectangular real matrices.

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: NumStability.Analysis.MatrixAlgebra exposes the identical compatible rectangular Frobenius product inequality; only the transparent P15 notation bridge is required. Mathlib also supplies Matrix.frobenius_norm_mul for these dimensions.

source_locations.anchor: prose listing the Frobenius norm's first useful property, ||AB|| <= ||A|| ||B||
source_locations.role: submultiplicative norm step used throughout the analysis

tier_rationale: The exact frozen-library theorem is NumStability.frobNormRect_rectMatMul_le in NumStability/Analysis/MatrixAlgebra.lean. The L proof only unfolds the transparent P15 rectangular product and Frobenius definitions.
